app.title: Speech Brain Viewer: speech-encoding receptive fields across auditory cortex
app.summary: A person picks whether to look at encoding-model results or at stimulation results, and in model mode picks which model or feature set to show. Recording sites appear on a 3D brain surface that they can rotate and zoom. Each site is coloured by its model correlation or by its anatomical area, and the rest of the brain can be hidden so only the temporal lobe shows. Clicking a site opens its fitted receptive field beside the brain. In stimulation mode, clicking a site shows the stimulation effect category and a written account of what happened.

task.text: Explore how well different speech-feature encoding models fit at each recording site across the brain, and open any site's fitted receptive field or stimulation result.

data.text: Recording sites with 3D anatomical coordinates and area labels. Each site has model-fit correlations for several models and fitted weights over time lags for each model's features. A table of stimulation effects per site has a category code and text descriptions.
data.item: a recording electrode on the cortical surface, with its fitted receptive fields and stimulation outcome

stage.text: exploring fitted encoding models across recording sites, as a companion to the published results

mechanism.text: A rotatable 3D brain surface shows every electrode coloured by the chosen model's correlation, by anatomy or by stimulation effect. Clicking an electrode redraws the linked side panel. In model mode the panel shows that electrode's receptive field: a heatmap of weights by feature and time lag, or a line for single-feature models. In stimulation mode it shows the effect descriptions. Dropdowns for result type and model drive both views at once.

field.text: spectrotemporal receptive field encoding models of intracranial recordings in auditory speech neuroscience

workflow.name: pick a site on a spatial layout and inspect its fitted model

steps.here: The 'Choose results to explore' dropdown switches between Receptive Fields and Stimulation. Stimulation mode hides the model and colour controls and swaps the side panel.

steps.step: choose the model or feature set to compare
steps.here: The 'Correlation type' dropdown picks spectrogram, full phonological+pitch, or the unique contribution of onset, peak rate, phonetic features, absolute pitch or relative pitch.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Every electrode is drawn on a 3D cortical mesh and coloured by the chosen model's correlation (diverging scale) or by anatomical area. A switch hides the whole brain so only the temporal lobe shows. Scrolling zooms and dragging rotates.

Hovering shows the anatomical label. Clicking an electrode draws its receptive field: a heatmap of beta weights by feature and time lag (-0.6 to 0 s), or a line for onset and peak rate. The title gives the r or unique r².

steps.step: read the outcome recorded for the item
steps.here: In stimulation mode, electrodes are coloured by a 1–3 effect code with a legend. Clicking one shows its passive-listening and repetition effect descriptions.

distinctive: The same model choice drives both the per-site colour on the brain and the receptive field drawn for the clicked site.
Feature-subset models report unique explained variance (unique r²), and the full models report a correlation r.

Receptive fields are drawn over time lags before the sound. Dashed lines split the feature groups (onset, peak rate, phonetic features, absolute pitch, relative pitch, change in relative pitch) or mark frequency bands.
A switch hides the rest of the brain so electrodes on the temporal lobe can be clicked more easily.
A second result type colours the same sites by a categorical stimulation effect and gives text descriptions in place of a fitted model.

parts.title: Result, model and display controls
parts.summary: Picks receptive fields or stimulation, the model whose correlation and weights are shown, how electrodes are coloured, and whether the whole brain or only the temporal lobe is drawn.

parts.title: 3D brain with electrodes
parts.summary: Shows every recording site on a rotatable cortical surface, coloured by model correlation, anatomy or stimulation effect, and clicking a site opens it in the side panel.

parts.title: Receptive field panel
parts.summary: Draws the clicked electrode's fitted weights for the chosen model, as a heatmap of feature by time lag or a line over time lag, with the fit score in the title.

parts.title: Stimulation effects panel
parts.summary: Explains the three stimulation effect categories and shows the passive-listening and repetition effect descriptions for the clicked electrode.

parts.title: Intro and brain-control notes
parts.summary: Explains what the viewer shows, how to rotate and zoom the brain, and the caveats about where electrodes are placed.
